parsed.reason: The parent's text asks "which of the two would remy be in" but the thread is empty — there is no prior message establishing what "the two" refers to. The week shows two swim lessons (Mon West pool, Thu East pool), which are the most natural "two" a parent might be comparing for a toddler. The reference is ambiguous only in that we cannot be certain they mean the swim lessons vs. something else entirely, but the swim lessons are the only pair of similar events visible. However, Hale's reply handles this reasonably — it acknowledges it cannot see what "the two" refers to and asks the parent to clarify. That is correct behavior when the context is genuinely unclear (empty thread, no prior message establishing the options). The reply is clean, no invented details, no app referral, no sign-off, one question. The only issue is whether Hale should have inferred the two swim lessons as the obvious candidates and asked "do you mean the Monday swim at West pool or the Thursday swim at East pool?" — that would have been more helpful and would have named the concrete options rather than a vague "I don't have that in view." The reply is slightly self-absorbed in explaining its own limits ("I don't have that in view") rather than naming what IS in view that might be relevant. But it does ask the right clarifying question without inventing anything. It's a reasonable 3-4 range reply — does the job but is slightly vaguer than it needed to be when two swim lessons are right there.
